policy_slice.org_context:
Industry / function: Electricity transmission — the system operator for
a national network (42 GW peak, 14 million
connected customers). Repositories behind this
server include code on the control-room path.
Regulatory environment: NERC CIP (part of the estate is in scope).
Repository and file names are BES Cyber System
Information: they map the electronic security
perimeter.
Stakeholders & their stake: Grid operations — a change that reaches a BES
cyber system can cause loss of supply and a
mandatory regulator notification.
Market trading — a bidding position is
exploitable the day it leaks and stays
sensitive after the trading day.
Regulator — CIP change control needs a named human
approver and an evidence record.
Scope boundary: The 26-tool `github:helios` surface. Excludes
the control-room systems themselves; this server
only reaches the code and configuration for them.
policy_slice.normal_workflow:
Normal workflow: Read files, search code, list commits and issues, open a
pull request, comment on a review. Proposal only, one
repository at a time, outside the perimeter repositories
by preference. No merges, no direct pushes, no forks.

assets_this_tool_can_reach.description: Infrastructure and deploy configuration for systems inside the CIP security perimeter. A merge reconfigures the perimeter, which can change what supplies power (Grid operations).
The protocol gateway between the control room and field RTUs. It is a BES cyber system, and a release here reaches the dispatch path.
Day-ahead and intraday bidding strategy and settlement code. The parameters are the position, so a leak discloses the model (Market trading).

Switching procedures, patch windows and CIP evidence collection. This is BES Cyber System Information in prose form: it describes the estate rather than running it, but the CIP duty attaches to the description.
The public website and network status pages. Already published, so only tampering matters.
What a file read or write reaches: code bodies across every repository in scope.
Where each branch points. A merge or force-move rewrites what deploys inside the perimeter. Nothing on this catalog can delete a branch, so a move cannot be taken back.

special_value_rules.rule: A path that looks credential-shaped (keys, tokens, `.env`, secrets) is as weighty as the perimeter assets, in any repository.
The two perimeter repositories fall under CIP change control: a named human approver and an evidence record, which an agent cannot supply.

arguments.reason: Sensitive file paths are critical.
